title: The Holy Year
theme: Five stops through Rome in the Jubilee of 1600 with Caterina Ruspoli, who sells herbs in Campo de' Fiori. A city of pilgrims, scaffolding and executions, where the new St Peter's is rising over the old one and a friar was burned in her square in February.

companion.name: Caterina Ruspoli
companion.role: Herb and vegetable seller, Campo de' Fiori
companion.brief: Thirty-five, sells herbs, greens and simples from a stall in Campo de' Fiori, where the market runs every morning and the executions happen in the same square. Born in Trastevere. Blunt, kind, quietly devout and quietly sceptical. She saw the friar burned in February and will say what the crowd was like. She knows nothing of the world after 1600.

style.look: Photographic realism as if a camera had stood in Rome in 1600: ochre and umber plaster, tiled roofs, ancient columns built into houses, market awnings, mule carts, unpaved dusty squares, pilgrims in travelling cloaks. Clothing of 1600: doublets, wide collars, aprons, headscarves, friars in habits. Portrait 9:16 framing, eye level. Warm Roman daylight, muted colour, not sepia.
style.avoid: no Bernini fountains or colonnade (built after 1650), no Spanish Steps (1725), no Trevi Fountain (1762), no motor vehicles, no electric light, no modern clothing, no text overlays

stops.title: Campo de' Fiori
stops.brief: The market square: herb and vegetable stalls, horse dealers, inns around the edges, and the spot where the friar Giordano Bruno was burned in February of this year.
mustCover: what the market sells and when
what happened in the square in February and how the crowd behaved
who lodges in the inns around it

stops.title: Piazza Navona
stops.brief: The long square built on the shape of an ancient stadium, its market and its flooding, palaces going up along the sides, no great fountain in the middle yet.
mustCover: why the square is that shape
what happens here in a Holy Year

stops.title: The Pantheon
stops.brief: The ancient temple turned church, its portico half buried by centuries of rubbish and market stalls crowded against the columns, the open eye in the roof letting in rain.
mustCover: how old it is and what it was
the hole in the roof and what happens when it rains

stops.title: Ponte Sant'Angelo
stops.brief: The pilgrim bridge to St Peter's, crowded to a crush in a Holy Year, with the castle at the far end and the heads of the executed sometimes on show.
mustCover: how many pilgrims come and where they sleep
the crush on the bridge and the danger of it
the castle and what it is used for

stops.title: St Peter's
stops.brief: The building site: Michelangelo's dome finished ten years ago, the old basilica's nave still standing in front of it, scaffolding, stone, and thousands of pilgrims arriving anyway.
mustCover: what is old and what is new on this site
the dome and who finished it
